First of all, let me say that I love this game idea, I think this is the nicest multiplayer bot game idea I've ever seen. And I've seen quite a lot of them. 

Reason: It's simple and easy to get started, the 2d array data structure is easy to think about, very few rules, but the game seems like it could also get very difficult. 

As expected from an unfinished product, there are still a few issues. Here are a few recommendations from me:

1) Adding to what darkhorse64 said, To make implementation easier, every player could always think that they are they player that starts at (0,0). Internally, you can mirror the board for every player so that this is true. Otherwise, everyone has to write this code.

2) "If a player goes on a position where the cell is not alive or steps off the grid, the player dies. If there are still two or more players alive after 150 frames, they are ranked by their mana." 
- Why not just run the simulation to completion? If the games are taking too long I think it would be better to just make the grid smaller. The last few turns are likely the most interesting. Also, with 192 tiles per player, it seems very possible for many players to survive, and mana is not a very good tiebreaker. 

3) For platforms, it's not clear that they will have a life value equal to the number of turns left from the input. (They should for convenience imo). To fix it, maybe go to the 'life' and 'dying' variables and change the description, I would personally also merge them into one variable like this (since it's not clear what life is when dying is false):

4) 'life': The number of turns until this cell disappears. 4 is the healthiest, 0 is dead. If the cell is not decaying, life is -1. (or 1000 instead of -1)

"strong" output: I don't see any rules that would make a cell strong, is this a future feature?

5) It seems like a passive strategy of trying to survive and not attacking at all would do much better than trying to attack people, which doesn't seem desirable. Maybe make bombs cheaper and/or dash more expensive? I haven't playtested it yet though so feel free to ignore this one if you've balanced these numbers out a lot

Hey ! I don't know how to edit the game page so i'll just write there I guess.

In this game, your character is a runner who moves on a grid composed of cells. Each cell dies shortly after the runner has stepped on it. The goal is to be the last one alive!

To help you achieve this goal, you can use various abilities with your mana, such as dashing, spawning a platform, or launching a bomb towards your enemies.

This game is currently in WIP so all the assets are probably going to change. If you have any suggestions or if you saw any bugs, do not hesitate to tell me, it will probably affect the final release of the game.

Thank you for taking the time to review my contribution. I updated the statement to fix all the errors that you pointed out. I hope that I have understood your feedback and fixed all the issues.

To clarify, game statements varies across different leagues as you unlock different abilities. Some information about bombs may not be relevant in the first league. However, I included these information so the code isn't reset between leagues. Let me know if this is not recommended.

As a non-native english speaker, any help you can provide in improving the grammar would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you for taking the time to review my contribution, you gave me the motivation to continue it lmao. I just updated it with minor changes, tho i have some question about what you said.

I don't understand the first point, since the board is not a square i can't rotate it for each player so ther all start at 0 0. If i adapt the code for each player so they think that they start at 0 0 regardless of their initial position, the bottom players might jump off the cells thinking that they started at the top of the board, and they have no way to tell.

For the second point, you are totally right and i'd like to run the simulation to more than 150 turn, but it's impossible with 4 players (max turn is 150). So I did some things to the game to make players die before the 150th turn. First, some cells randomly decay, this is also to prevent player from doing the exact same game if they start at the same position. The decaying speed highly increase from turn 120 to 150. I don't really like it to be honest because the end of the game is more based on luck, but it's the best i had. Then, the bombs highly decrease the number of cells, they can one shot 21 cells in a single turn, so it's unlikeley that high ranked players end up in a tie. I deleted the part where players are ranked by their mana at the end, if two or more players survive, it will be a tie, wich force them to play more agressively to get the first place. Thank you for this suggestion :D

For the 3rd and 4th point i'll probably merge the dying and life indeed, but i may implement feature such as cells that can be not max life and not dying, so for now i'll keep it. This will be decided when i'll post the game for validation.

the "strong" thing is not affordant in the statement, i updated it. To clarify it's the platform cells that are considered "strong".

For the fifth point, i decreased the cost of all spells to 10. For the dash because i think it's the right cost, for the platform because even tho the spell is strong, you want to use it with a dash 90% of the time, so the combo still end up costing 20. And for the bomb, i think the cost of it should be the same as the dash, because you need a dash to get out of it. I don't know if this is the right balance, i definitely need testers especially in the 4th league so i can see the things that are op or bad.

One last thing, for the spells cost i had the idea to randomize the cost of each spells each games, so you have to decide your strategy depending on that (for example if dash cost 20 and bomb 5 then you want to play agressively) I don't know if that's a good idea and i don't think i'll implement it except if a lot of people like it.

Anyway thank you again for your review

Here are some more suggestions after playtesting:

1) n_row is 35 and n_col is 22, but the image has 22 rows and 35 columns. Every time I use x, y coordinates, I personally get things messed up, because x represents the column index and y represents the row index, which makes all correct code feel like the loop order is backwards. Maybe change n_rows and n_cols to y_length and x_length?

2) Cell coordinates don't really need x,y coordinates as input, you can just say that they are both 0 indexed instead (otherwise i=x and j=y in code).

3) There is a minor typo in the output, MOVE says "the four possibles directions" instead of "the four possible directions"

4) The way that cell life is displayed is confusing, I notice that when you walk onto a cell it has life 3, then this ticks down to 2, 1, 0, and then the cell dies. In particular, there is one frame during which the cell life is 0 but the cell still exists, and there is no way to distinguish this from a dead cell.
I only noticed this because when cells under the bomb get life=0 the turn before the bomb explodes. Even the cell my player is on gets life=0, which was causing my code to crash. 
It's also a little bit surprising that the tile you start on doesn't decay, but it's not really a problem.

5) The text for dying should probably be changed to
"dying 1 if the cell is decaying or dead, 0 otherwise." instead of "dying 1 if the cell is decaying, 0 otherwise."

6) Might be helpful to have some extra response time on the first turn beyond 50ms - I didn't run into any issues but a lot of code does extra preprocessing at the start.

7) If you can make 'replay in same conditions' use the same seed for the AI and random cell destruction, it would be helpful for debugging

8) Speaking of debugging, I don't think there is an error message for code timeout

9) I also managed to crash the game. I was printing "SPELL DASH right" instead of "SPELL DASH right 4", that might have done it, though it was working fine in league 2: https://www.codingame.com/replay/723076723

I fixed the things you pointed out in the three first point and all the typo mistakes. For the fourth one, this bug was occuring because of the order of action in the game code. Before, it was bomb update -> cell update -> input sent to player -> player update -> check for dead players. Now it' input sent to player -> player update -> bomb update -> cell update -> check for dead players wich is way better. The only downside of this is if you want to debug the game frame by frame using the left and right key. You might get weird informations like a cell that is dead being displayed as 1hp. This is because when you debug this way the informations that you printed in the console are the informations that the player got before the cells got updated, and the informations you see graphically are the informations after the cells got updated. From a code point of view this is the best way to do it but for debugging it's kinda confusing.

The "replay in same condition" work for the random cell destructtions, but the AI are coded with random, wich is bad for this feature. I did this because since the first AI are supposed to be dumb they always ended up on the same cells at some point without random, and then doing the exact same movements. I have to find a way to prevent this without random so the "replay in same condition" work. I didn't fix this yet but i'll work on it.

For the extra time response it's supposed to be already coded (100ms for the first round instead of 50ms) but i don't really know if it work since i have no way to test it.

And finally for the crash i was unable to crash my game with this method. This is really weird since the code where the crash happened is in a "try" block, so it shouldn't crash at all even with an error. If you manage to do it again d not hesitate to share it with me.

Anyway thx again for all theses feedbacks this is really helping to finih the game.

The main things i want to work on before publishing the game (not including bug fixes) are the graphics and the AI, idealy i would like to have 7 AI (three wood league, bronze, silver, gold, legend) even if community games can only have wood leagues they will act as if they were actually above wood. Also the league 4 AI is broken, it was able to dodge bombs because of the bug of the 4th point but now that it's fix they are unable to dodge.
With the reduced price of bombs, the games hardly get above round 100 (even with ai that can dodge bombs) because they remove so much cells, so i don't think the number of cells should be reduced.
